questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. Using a two-way table, find the probability of a sum of 7, of a double, and of a sum of at least 10. Explain why the eleven possible sums are not equally likely.
questions.expected_answer: The table has 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely cells. A sum of 7 fills six cells (1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4, 4 and 3, 5 and 2, 6 and 1), so the probability is 6 over 36, which is 1 over 6. A double fills the six cells on the main diagonal, also 1 over 6. A sum of at least 10 fills three cells with 10, two with 11 and one with 12, six cells, 1 over 6. The sums are not equally likely because different sums fill different numbers of cells: a sum of 2 fills one cell, probability 1 over 36, while 7 fills six, so treating the eleven sums as 1 over 11 each is wrong.

questions.question: A spinner is one third red and two thirds blue and is spun twice. Draw the tree diagram and find the probability of two reds, of two blues, and of one of each colour. Show the check that the tips add to 1.
questions.expected_answer: First spin: red 1 over 3, blue 2 over 3; second spin from each end: the same two branches. Red-red: 1 over 3 × 1 over 3 = 1 over 9. Red-blue: 1 over 3 × 2 over 3 = 2 over 9. Blue-red: 2 over 9. Blue-blue: 2 over 3 × 2 over 3 = 4 over 9. Check: 1 over 9 + 2 over 9 + 2 over 9 + 4 over 9 = 9 over 9 = 1. One of each colour is red-blue or blue-red: 2 over 9 + 2 over 9 = 4 over 9.

questions.question: A bag has 3 red and 2 green marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are red and that they are different colours. Then find the probability of two reds if the first marble is replaced, and explain the difference.
questions.expected_answer: Without replacement: first red 3 over 5; then 2 red and 2 green remain, so second red 2 over 4. P(red, red) = 3 over 5 × 2 over 4 = 6 over 20 = 3 over 10. Green-green = 2 over 5 × 1 over 4 = 2 over 20 = 1 over 10. Different colours = 1 − 3 over 10 − 1 over 10 = 6 over 10 = 3 over 5 (or red-green 6 over 20 plus green-red 6 over 20). With replacement the bag is unchanged for the second draw, so P(red, red) = 3 over 5 × 3 over 5 = 9 over 25, which is larger than 3 over 10 because the red marble drawn first is available again for the second draw.
